transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, hi. Thanks. So, what brings me in... well, it's been a whole thing. I'm an electrician, right? Mostly commercial stuff, some residential, and I usually handle a lot of the backend paperwork along with the actual wiring. But what finally got me to actually come in here and sit down with you is that I just... I can’t keep my focus on one estimate or code form anymore. 

It's like my brain is just constantly jumping around. I’ll sit down at my desk to fill out a permit or do a load calculation—stuff I learned years ago, you know, basic stuff I've done a million times—but then I'll hear a tool noise from the guys out in the workshop, like a drill firing up or a compressor, or I'll get a random text message on my phone, or I'll just suddenly get this completely new idea about how we need to redesign the workshop layout to be more efficient. And the second that happens, I'm completely pulled off track. I have to go check the tool, or answer the text, or start sketching out the new workshop idea right that second. 

And then when I finally get back to what I was actually supposed to be doing, the jobs start getting all mixed up. I'll have the blueprints for a restaurant remodel tangled up with a residential panel upgrade, and I'm messing up the quotes because I'm pulling numbers from the wrong page. It's just... everything is pulling my attention all at once and I can't get anything straight.
Have you noticed any periods where you felt unusually energized, needed less sleep, or were more talkative or productive than usual?

Energized? Yeah, I mean, absolutely. It's funny you ask that because, honestly, I've been going completely nonstop lately. Like, a hundred miles an hour, constantly. Usually, a guy gets pretty wiped out after a full day of electrical work, but lately I’ll go straight from roughing in a whole job site—pulling wire, drilling studs, all the heavy physical stuff—and instead of taking a breather or grabbing lunch, I’m instantly driving across town to knock out three different bids for new clients. 

And then I get back to the shop, and I can't just clock out and go home. I’ve been staying in the workshop rewiring all our test panels. The other guys think I'm crazy, but I just... I have to keep my hands moving. I’ve also gotten super into these new home-automation setups recently, right? Smart switches, integrated relays, tying everything into a central hub, that kind of stuff. I’ll start mocking up one idea, getting all the components out on the bench, but before I even have the first one halfway done, my brain is already on the next concept and I'm starting a completely new automation layout right next to it. 

It’s just... sitting still physically bothers me right now. It literally feels like I’m wasting time if I’m not doing something productive. There are only so many hours in the day, and when you feel like you can just keep going and going, why would you sit on the couch? So yeah, I’m just bouncing from the sites, to the bids, to the workshop, over and over, just trying to get it all out.

Have you noticed any distinct periods — maybe a few days or more — where your mood was either unusually high, euphoric, or irritable, where you felt like you were on top of the world or maybe even easily annoyed or agitated, and this was clearly different from your usual self?

Yeah, actually, that’s... that’s exactly it. It’s like I get into this zone where I just feel incredible, you know? Like I’m completely on top of everything. I’ll be in this huge, pumped-up mood, just feeling like I’ve got the golden ticket. Like the other day, I was at the shop, and I was just going on and on to the guys about how we need to pivot the whole business model. I was telling them, look, we’re doing okay with the standard commercial and residential, but the real money, the real future, is in solar integration. I was laying out this whole master plan about how our little shop is going to become the main solar outfit in the entire town. I mean, I had the whole thing mapped out in my head—the supply chains, the marketing, the training we’d need to do. I was so hyped about it, just feeling like a genius, honestly. 

But then... well, the flip side of that is the irritability you mentioned. Because when I’m in that headspace, when everything is so clear to me and I’m just firing on all cylinders, I have zero patience for anyone slowing me down. If my wife asks me a simple question about the budget for this big solar idea, or if one of the apprentices at the shop hesitates or questions the plan, I just... I can just flip. Like, a switch goes off. I get so sharp with them, snapping over absolutely nothing. I’ll just bite their heads off because it feels like they’re dragging their feet or they just don’t get the vision, you know? And it’s not like me to be that harsh, usually I’m a pretty easygoing boss and husband, but lately, if you’re not on my level and moving at my speed, I just get so incredibly annoyed and agitated. It’s like I’m this unstoppable force, and they’re just these annoying roadblocks in my way.

latest_inference.note: The patient described distinct periods of abnormally elevated mood, increased energy, decreased need for rest, and irritability when interrupted—consistent with bipolar I disorder, current episode hypomanic. Other candidates (F90.0, F32.9, F33.9) were ruled out based on the presence of a clear hypomanic episode rather than unipolar depression or ADHD alone.
